Alpha 1.79.22 (Actor lighting correctness)

  • Procedural fallback characters and Skeletons retain correct surface lighting when a stretched animation hierarchy produces shear. Unsupported transforms use the original mesh renderer rather than the instance shader’s inaccurate normal approximation; normal rotations and ordinary nonuniform scale retain batching.
  • Live animation and equipment transforms remain responsive. Original materials, triangles, visibility and shadow behavior are retained, including returning to batching when a pose becomes supported again.
  • Focused native High/Low comparisons cover Skeletons and ten fully equipped procedural characters spanning all four classes. Existing pixel, triangle and visibility limits remain unchanged. Unsupported poses intentionally retain original draw counts; this is a correctness fix, not a frame-rate claim.
  • Supplied rigged GLBs, fitted equipment, gameplay, rewards and saved progress remain unchanged. Full modern-world art, equipped-party and physical-device qualification remain ongoing; raised terrain is still disabled by default.
  • Full prior patch history is retained; login shows ten notes initially with Load more notes.

Alpha 1.79.21 (Working town details)

  • Lanternhold’s common well has an open wooden bucket, iron bands and bail, a winding drum, rope and crank. Its existing stone basin, safe-zone recovery, walking space and ambient worker behavior are retained.
  • Courtyard benches use separated timber slats with modest beveled edges and back supports. The same thirteen walking footprints, material batches and scene-owned resource cleanup remain; no new obstacles, texture maps or per-frame animation work.
  • Votive Market gains curved provision casks with iron hoops under its canopy. Casks and the supply chest meet the actual stone platform; stacked shipping crates meet each other rather than overlapping or sinking into the plinth. Existing market bounds, services and walking routes remain unchanged.
  • The town review uses the delivered dressed Archmage Ilyra appearance rather than an inaccurate bare player Wizard stand-in. This corrects the review scene; the live story NPC already uses that outfit.
  • Credits & notices on login opens a small, script-free page linking the original browser-library, Cinzel font and four supplied character-source notices, plus Ilyra’s source information. It does not load game models or grant a new project license.
  • Native visual QA retains character, environment and celebration screenshots separately, so later release-smoke commands do not erase them. Existing checks, render limits and optional/full-test choices are unchanged; retained evidence is scanned before upload.
  • This scoped town refinement is not final modern-world art, equipped-party or physical-device acceptance. Original rendering limits remain unchanged. Raised terrain remains disabled by default; broader world, character and performance work continues.
  • Supplied class, equipment and animation assets, gameplay, rewards, permissions and saved progress remain unchanged. Full prior patch history is retained; login shows ten notes initially with Load more notes.

Alpha 1.79.20 (Pilgrim camps and worn streets)

  • Lanternhold camps have folded leather bedrolls with rolled ends instead of floating boxes. Hearth stones meet the ground and firewood stacks physically, using existing timber and leather material batches.
  • Charcoal follows each actual rotated hearth, and compacted ground connects tent entrances to their hearths. Both are baked into the existing ground mask: no decals, extra textures, draw calls or per-frame work.
  • Town roads use larger irregular flagstones instead of uniform brick-like paving. Unequal courses, chipped corners and short worn fractures share one periodic layout across color, relief and roughness. High and Low preserve the same slab sizes and joints, without new textures, geometry or shader samples.
  • All 15 camp placements, rotations, nine material batches, walking blockers and service paths remain unchanged. The detailed camp props add 3,300 raw triangles across the entire town; original reference-view budgets remain unchanged.
  • Native High/Low equipped town views qualify this scoped update, not final modern-world art, sustained equipped-party or physical-device performance. Raised terrain remains disabled by default; broader art and performance work continues.
  • Supplied actor, equipment and animation assets, combat, rewards, account permissions and saved progress remain unchanged. Full prior patch history is retained; login shows ten notes initially with Load more notes.

Alpha 1.79.19 (Grounded town and regional materials)

  • Lanternhold pilgrim tents have folded ridge canvas, open curtains, timber frames and supported lanterns. Their buried origin is corrected while the 15 horizontal camp placements and existing walking blockers remain unchanged.
  • Generated administrator teleport-clearance data matches the corrected camp height. Only those 15 vertical bounds change; horizontal walls, service approaches and all other landing geometry remain unchanged.
  • Tents, banners and regional sails share physical canvas thread detail that filters away below pixel resolution. Existing colors, lighting and material batches remain; there are no additional cloth textures or per-frame cloth simulation. Air windbreak corners now meet their support posts and crossbars.
  • Earth soil has finer aggregate detail and quieter broad contrast. Existing plants gain deterministic variation in breadth and height, while preserving every placement, horizontal clearance, Low subset, plant tones and rooted wind bounds.
  • Cinder Wastes ground uses a roughly nine-metre basalt and ash scale with restrained contrast. Kiln Span and Molten Approach supports gain staggered worn basalt courses inside their existing collision footprints.
  • Regional lore books gain curved paper stacks and writing that follows the fold. Their desks, bindings, quest markers and inspection bounds are retained; fewer page and writing meshes are submitted.
  • Foliage visibility and shadow restoration reuse frame-local arrays instead of rebuilding hash sets. Eligibility, exact bounds, live actors and end-of-frame restoration stay unchanged.
  • Original frame, draw and triangle limits remain unchanged. Bounded native High/Low world views and equipped town captures qualify this update, not final modern-world, equipped-party, physical-device or campaign acceptance. Raised terrain remains disabled by default; no experimental outcrop-shader rollout.
  • Supplied actor, equipment and animation assets, class restrictions, combat, rewards and saved player data remain unchanged. Full prior patch history is retained; login initially shows ten notes with a load-more control.

Alpha 1.79.18 (Air Realm scenery and lighting)

  • Gale cypresses gain curved rooted trunks, fuller needle crowns and matching bark instead of cylinders and detached root cones. All 90 existing tree placements, instance scales, rotations and collision clearances are retained.
  • Air ground detail uses a roughly nine-metre material scale and sheltered dust pockets rather than broad repeated diagonal deposits. Color, relief and roughness still share three registered surface maps; the floor remains flat.
  • Weather instruments have forged pointer silhouettes, bearings and calibrated instrument bands. Observatory chart tables gain grounded legs and bracing within their existing footprints.
  • Courier shelving gains timber supports. Bivouacs have padded, folded canvas bedrolls with rolled ends instead of solid boxes; they join the existing canvas material batch, without new materials or textures.
  • Air lighting uses stronger directional light and less ambient wash to shape stone, cloth and equipment. Existing light counts, colors, exposure, fog and bloom settings are retained.
  • Original frame, draw and triangle limits pass in bounded native High/Low reference views. Quality switching retains foliage transforms, materials and scene ownership. Prior failed profiles remain recorded; this is not whole-game performance certification.
  • This is combined regional component polish, not final modern-world approval, equipped-party or physical-device qualification, the 1.80 feature freeze or full 1.87 completion. Raised terrain remains disabled in the public world.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, combat, quest, economy or permission change. Supplied class/equipment source models remain unchanged. Full prior patch history is preserved through Load more notes.

Alpha 1.79.17 (Air Realm passage composition)

  • Air Realm travel gains broken roadside heath and scree, with spatial groundcover cells that share existing materials and receive shadows without adding solid obstacles.
  • Existing gale cypresses frame more of the main passage before filling side stands. Tree counts, stable identities, per-tree scale and rotation remain unchanged; paths, landmarks, hazards and portal approaches keep their clearances.
  • High and Low detail retain deterministic placement subsets. Changing quality redraws the appropriate foliage and groundcover without replacing their owning scene groups, materials or transforms.
  • Earth, Water and Fire placements, supplied class and equipment models, gameplay, collisions, quest targets and saved player data remain unchanged. Original frame, draw and triangle limits remain required.
  • This is incremental route composition, not final modern-world approval, equipped-party or physical-device qualification, the 1.80 feature freeze or full 1.87 completion. Raised terrain remains disabled in the public world.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, currency or permission change. Full prior patch history is preserved through Load more notes.

Alpha 1.79.16 (worn masonry, woodland shading and shared enemy rendering)

  • The First Grove vault follows a curved stone profile with shallow carved lips on both faces. Its original overhead clearance, footprint, depth and shared fieldstone material remain unchanged.
  • Grove and Bastion pier courses have worn corners and staggered masonry joints instead of monolithic slices. Existing material batching is retained; no new textures or runtime draw buckets are added.
  • Natural stone gains continuous mineral grain, sheltered lichen and damp lower courses. Detail follows world space across curved faces and fades below pixel size rather than painting another brick grid over the vault.
  • Nearby Skeletons share opaque render batches across their independently animated rigs, reducing repeated color and shadow draws without removing enemies or changing their surfaces, animations or hitboxes. Supplied class models and unreviewed enemy families keep their existing rendering path.
  • Bent woodland leaves have continuous lighting across their sections and subtle plant-to-plant tones instead of identical repeated colors. Existing plants, silhouettes, triangle counts, placements, wind and walking clearances remain unchanged.
  • Area cleanup releases each instanced mesh's matrix and color buffers as well as its shared geometry, preventing those owned GPU buffers from accumulating across area changes.
  • Collision, paths, quest targets, planted roots, thresholds and gameplay rules stay unchanged. Original geometry and scene performance limits remain required.
  • This is incremental landmark refinement, not final modern-world approval, equipped-party or physical-device qualification, the 1.80 feature freeze or full 1.87 completion. Raised terrain remains disabled in the public world.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, currency or permission change. Full prior patch history is preserved through Load more notes.

Alpha 1.79.15 (scenery rendering and atlas detail)

  • Owned, unchanged scene containers and foliage groups avoid repeated local matrix composition and unnecessary static world-matrix multiplication. Actors, bones, equipment animations, moved parents and reparented scenery remain live.
  • The foliage registry visits registered scenery instead of unrelated character rigs and buildings. Cell bounds and frustum results are reused only for exact current transforms, bounds, camera, light and shadow-filter inputs. No movement thresholds or timed approximations are introduced.
  • Irrelevant direct foliage cells skip eligibility work, while nested scenery and live region, material and visibility changes retain their existing behavior. Pointer targeting reuses each actor's owned interaction box instead of repeatedly searching its fitted rig; detached or replaced boxes fall back to normal lookup.
  • Ordinary world frames no longer search the entire scene for a casino interior that is not present. Casino doors and floors reuse their current owned scene roots, reacquire replacements and release references on cleanup. Seating, floor visibility, table timers and wagers are unchanged.
  • The atlas uses distinct engraved birch, pine, willow, deadwood, briar, wind-bent cypress and storm-crystal symbols at their existing world locations. Roads, gates, destinations, phone controls and cached map sizes are unchanged.
  • Generated groundcover keeps its fixed local transform while shader wind and live instance transforms remain active. Detached scenery and disposed renderers restore their original methods and remove owned listeners.
  • Geometry, density, shadows, cell sizes, filter margins, quality settings, collisions, gameplay and frame budgets remain unchanged. Raised terrain remains disabled in the public world; final equipped-party, device, modern-art and feature-freeze qualification remain open.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, economy or permission change. Full prior patch history is preserved through Load more notes.

Alpha 1.79.14 (character surfaces and constructed dungeon interiors)

  • All 252 supplied wearable fits now have registered High/Low detail selections. Reduced copies preserve source identities, rigging and fit; 32 unchanged variants reuse originals. Missing copies fall back to the registered original and record the affected slot. Supplied source assets remain unchanged.
  • Supplied equipment gains shared cloth, leather, wood and metal surface detail while preserving authored textures, colors and magical accents. Only eligible materials with usable UVs receive the generated maps; compatible equipment still batches together.
  • Robes and skirts hide enclosed underwear and body hips. Robes also mask fully concealed upper trouser armor without removing visible lower legs, crossing triangles or exposed skirt waistbands. Outfit changes restore the original layers; supplied GLBs and other characters are unchanged.
  • The game world and character preview now share filmic highlight handling. Existing lighting, exposure, quality controls and passes are retained.
  • Dungeon vigils have stepped feet, profiled shafts and forged cages; reliquary coffers gain vaulted lids and straps, and restorative fonts have hollow basins. Existing shared materials and room batching are reused.
  • All five dungeon themes have varied, worn flagstones with registered physical surface detail. Compact room markers leave the combat floor readable while preserving objective, reward, cleared-room and exit feedback. Floors stay flat; collisions, layout, encounter and reward rules are unchanged.
  • This is an integrated polish pass, not final modern-art approval or the 1.80 feature freeze. Raised terrain, equipped-party/device qualification and full 1.87 remain staged. No account wipe, schema migration or economy change. Full prior patch history is preserved through Load more notes.

Alpha 1.79.13 (optional public outage monitoring)

  • The existing outage monitor can optionally check the public login page, frontend release manifest and backend health over normal HTTPS, in addition to its local API and database check.
  • Public checks require matching frontend/backend/local release identities and a ready database, with bounded response sizes, one shared public deadline and no redirects or forced IPv4. These checks verify HTTP structure, not full browser gameplay or off-machine coverage.
  • Both public endpoint settings default to empty. Paired configuration is checked before replacing the game service; invalid or incomplete public settings fail closed. Existing installed monitoring remains local-only until an operator explicitly configures and restarts the matching monitor artifact.
  • The existing alert recipients, three-failure/two-success debounce, reminder limits, email provider and retention remain unchanged. The operator guide explains same-artifact rollback and release-transition qualification before enabling public alerts.
  • No account wipe, schema migration, retention, economy, quest or Dark Realm access changes. Full 1.80 freeze, operations ownership, off-machine backup, modern-art and beta gates remain open. Full prior patch history is preserved through Load more notes.
